To determine the effect of adding a substance to a buffer solution, first identify whether the species is an electrolyte (dissolves in water) or a non-electrolyte (does not dissolve in water) based on its solubility.
If the species does dissolve, identify whether the species produces spectator ions, acidic or basic species, or ions that are already components of the buffer system.

Then remember that spectator ions do not change the equilibrium and have no effect on concentrations of the components of the buffer system. Acidic species react with the basic component of the buffer, reducing the concentrations of the basic component and hydroxide while increasing the concentration of the acidic component of the buffer. Likewise, basic species will react with the acidic component of the buffer, reducing the concentrations of the acidic component and hydronium while increasing the concentration of the basic component of the buffer.
